standard.title: Geosynthetics — Guidelines for Installation of Geotexiles as Pavement Fabric
standard.description: This standard prescribes guidelines for the installation of geotextiles as pavement fabric (paving fabric) inside road pavements to provide waterproofing, stress relief, and barrier separation, thereby retarding reflective cracking in asphalt concrete overlays.
standard.scope: This standard prescribes guidelines for the installation of geotextiles as pavement fabric (paving fabric) inside road pavements to provide waterproofing, stress relief, and barrier separation, thereby retarding reflective cracking in asphalt concrete overlays.

certification.description: Statutory Voluntary Guideline for Installation, but under the mandatory 'Geotextiles (Quality Control) Order' (issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India), the geotextile/geosynthetic materials (pavement fabrics) themselves must conform to Indian Standards and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Laying pavement fabrics without certified materials is a punishable statutory offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic polymer paving fabrics.
requirements: During installation, the paving fabric must be rolled out such that the fuzzy (heat-bonded or non-woven lofted) side of the paving fabric is laid down directly into the hot asphalt tack coat, leaving the smooth side facing up.
The tack coat application rate must be sufficient to saturate the geotextile fabric and form a waterproof bond with the existing pavement surface. Solvents and cutbacks must not be used.

Cationic and anionic asphalt emulsions may be used successfully, provided: a) The paving fabric is laid only after allowing the specified time for curing (break) of the emulsion; b) No traffic is allowed over the area where the tack coat is applied; and c) They are applied at a higher rate to compensate for the water content.

In zones of heavy vehicle braking—including street intersections, steep grades, and deceleration lanes—the normal tack coat application rate must be reduced by approximately 20 percent as directed by the engineer to prevent fabric slippage or fatting-up of asphalt.

When encountering drains, manholes, joints, or other road irregularities, the geotextile must be placed normally and then cut cleanly around the obstruction. Any wrinkles exceeding 25 mm must be slit open and flatly overlapped.

Prior to applying the asphalt concrete (AC) overlay, the laid geotextile must be formally inspected by a certified inspector of the engineer to verify that the fabric has suffered zero installation damage. Damaged geotextile must be immediately repaired or replaced.

The geotextile must be utilized to rehabilitate localized distressed areas, utility cuts, and excessively cracked pavement prior to an AC overlay, using either a full-width layer or targeted membrane strips depending on distress severity.
